name: Question 11
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=(2t+1)^{3}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{65}{8}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t+1)^{3}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{65}{8}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{65}{8} & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot {[2(1)+1]}^{4}+C \\ \frac{65}{8} & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (81)+C \\ C & =\frac{65}{8}-\frac{81}{8} \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}-2.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}(2t+1)^{4}-2 & =0 \\ (2t+1)^{4} & =16 \\ 2t+1 & =\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $t=-\frac{3}{2}\,,\frac{1}{2}.$

Since $t>0$, we discard solution $t=-\frac{3}{2}.$ 
Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{s}.$

Question 11
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=(2t+1)3, where t>0 is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=658m/s when t=1s, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

a
t=12s
b
t=3s
c
t=32s
d
t=1s
e
t=2s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The particle is stationary when v=0m/s.

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(2t+1)3dt=18(2t+1)4+C To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=658. Substituting this into the above gives 658=18⋅[2(1)+1]4+C658=18⋅(81)+CC=658−818C=−2. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=18(2t+1)4−2.

Now, we find the moments in time when v=0m/s:

18(2t+1)4−2=0(2t+1)4=162t+1=±2.

The solutions are t=−32,12.

Since t>0, we discard solution t=−32. Therefore, the particle is stationary when t=12s.
